measurement_protocol.rate_unit: million complete interior-cell updates per second
measurement_protocol.rate_range_definition: observed minimum and maximum of useful_updates / each raw seconds value
measurement_protocol.range_interpretation: Observed extrema of twelve individual rates; these ranges are not confidence intervals.
measurement_protocol.pairing: The repeat index and original within-pair implementation order are retained.
measurement_protocol.timer_scope: One complete ordered device graph replay, including every required numerical stage and state publication
measurement_protocol.physical_update: A shallow-water update includes all three fields, both time stages and periodic boundaries. An energy-balance update includes both time stages and pole copies.
measurement_protocol.precision: Ordered binary64 arithmetic with contraction and fast-math disabled; canonical output agreement is checked outside the timer.

power_policy.benchmark_policy: The native benchmark did not set power limits or clocks. Recorded samples include automatic clock and power management.

quiet_policy.allocation: One owned exclusive node; only the current numerical step and the declared idle batch step are allowed.
quiet_policy.placement: The host driver is pinned to CPU1 and NUMA node0; the selected GPU UUID is fixed.
quiet_policy.post_sample_observation: GPU process ownership and host load are checked after each timed graph; the full observations remain in the hashed timing evidence.
quiet_policy.clock_and_power_management: The native benchmark did not set power limits or clocks. Recorded samples include automatic clock and power management.
quiet_policy.acceptance: All six retained conditions have accepted exclusive-node and quiet-sample flags; automatic clock or software power-cap events are disclosed separately.

scope: The cohorts use separate runs and nodes. Comparisons show recorded absolute rates and do not establish a freshly paired speedup.
CPU rates use complete-run wall time on one Neoverse V2 core. GPU rates use complete-graph CUDA event time on one GH200 device.
Compilation, setup and verification are excluded. GPU transfers and graph construction are also excluded.
The workload grids, batch lengths and retained input generators agree. Each cohort passed its own recorded physical and exact-output checks.
Python is compiled with Numba. These records do not describe interpreted Python.

Original cohort checks apply. Historical GPU evidence covers final and last first-stage states, without the newer complete current, preceding and stage-buffer gate. Original CPU checks and original grid-dependent batch lengths are retained. These records are not labelled as newly matched 1,000-step runs.
The separately dated 12 November Summary uses the unchanged current matched input and its own stronger acceptance.

sw.caption_text: Rates retain the original seven-row comparison. ESM.md uses the Fortran runs from 8 November 2026 on nid010573, job 8199657. The six language controls use October runs on nid011277 (CPU, job 7072889) or nid010353 (GPU, job 7143612). CPU results use one Neoverse V2 core and GPU results use one GH200 device. Points are the saved medians of twelve individual rates, with observed minimum and maximum whiskers. The cohorts use separate runs and nodes, so these bars do not establish a freshly paired speedup. Python is compiled with Numba. Each facet has an independent zero-based linear rate axis. These comparisons remain separate from the 12 November matched primary measurements.

takeaways: 12 Nov ESM.md CPU rates are 90.9–97.3% of baseline.
12 Nov ESM.md GPU rates are 90.5–103.2% of baseline.
12 Nov pairs use up to 248 CPU cores or one GPU.
